transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been having these strange moments where things don’t feel real. Like, I’ll be in my own house or at my office, and it feels almost like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. It’s been unsettling.
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in activities, or noticing changes in your sleep or appetite around the same time these strange moments started?

Yeah… I wouldn’t say I’m just sad all the time, exactly, but I’ve noticed I can’t really enjoy things. My wife will try to joke with me, or she’ll bring up going fishing like we had planned, and I know that should feel good. It just doesn’t. It’s like that part of me is switched off right now.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like fishing with your wife, don’t bring you the same pleasure anymore?

Yes. That’s exactly it. My wife will joke around with me, or mention the fishing trip we’d planned, and I know I’d normally enjoy that. But right now it just doesn’t land. It feels like the part of me that’s supposed to feel good about those things is kind of shut off.
Has this loss of enjoyment affected most of the activities you used to like, or is it mostly limited to certain situations?

It’s mostly the things I used to look forward to. Like my wife trying to joke with me, or talking about our fishing trip… I know those should make me feel good, but they just don’t. It’s like that part of me that enjoys them is switched off right now.
Has this lack of enjoyment in things you used to like been happening almost every day, and does it last for most of the day?

Yeah, pretty much. It’s been there most days. My wife will try to joke with me, or bring up going fishing like we planned, and I know normally that would feel good. But most of the day it’s like that part of me is just switched off.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, or like you don’t have the energy to do things, even things that wouldn’t normally drain you?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve felt off, but I can’t say I’ve noticed being unusually tired or drained in a clear way. Not more than I’d expect, I guess.
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not worth much or feeling guilty about things more than usual?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t really been feeling worthless or unusually guilty. I mean, I’ve been shaken up, but not in that way.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating more or less than usual?
I haven’t really noticed a clear change there. My appetite seems about the same, and I don’t think my weight has changed much, at least not that I can tell.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?
No, I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed most of the day nearly every day. I’ve had moments where I feel upset or not like myself, but it doesn’t feel like being down all day like that.
Can you describe what you mean by things not feeling real? Have you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings during these moments?

Yeah… it’s like I’ll be sitting in my own house, or at my office, and suddenly it just doesn’t feel real. Like I know where I am, but it feels distant or off somehow.

Sometimes it’s almost like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. It’s unsettling, because I know it’s my life and my surroundings, but in those moments I feel kind of detached from it.
Have these feelings of things not feeling real or feeling detached from yourself happened even when you weren’t feeling down or upset?

Yes. It’s not only when I’m upset. Sometimes I’ll be at home or in my office and, out of nowhere, it feels like the place isn’t real, or like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. It’s strange, because I know where I am, but it feels disconnected.
Have you used any substances, medications, or experienced any medical issues around the time these feelings of detachment started?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed any medical issue around when it started, and I’m not sure about anything specific that would explain it. Nothing obvious comes to mind.
Have you experienced these feelings of detachment or things not feeling real even when you weren’t feeling down or upset?

Yes, it happens even when I’m not especially upset or feeling down. I’ll be in my house or at work, and it just feels unreal all of a sudden. Like I’m there, but not really there… almost like I’m watching myself from across the room.
Have you ever felt like you were outside of your body, or like you were watching yourself from a distance, beyond what you've already described?

Yes… I mean, that’s probably the part that bothers me most. It’s like I’m in my own house or sitting in my office, but suddenly I feel like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being in my body. I know I’m there, but it feels unreal and distant.
